title: Server: add SupportMessage model + enums to Prisma schema and migrate
description:
Add a new model for user-submitted bug reports / general messages to the app team, following the exact style of `FieldIssueReport` (server/prisma/schema.prisma:177-199).

1. Add two new enums, placed near the other small status enums (e.g. right after `FieldIssueStatus` at schema.prisma:169-172):
```prisma
enum SupportMessageType {
  BUG
  FEEDBACK
}

enum SupportMessageStatus {
  OPEN
  RESOLVED
}
```

2. Add the model itself, placed near the other report-style models (e.g. right after `FieldReport` at schema.prisma:235-249, before `model Game`):
```prisma
/// A user-submitted bug report or general message to the app team, surfaced
/// to admins under /admin (web) and /admin (mobile). Not tied to a specific
/// Field or Game -- this is app-wide feedback, unlike FieldIssueReport.
model SupportMessage {
  id        String               @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  type      SupportMessageType
  message   String
  /// Optional free-text context the client can attach (e.g. current screen/route,
  /// app version) to help debugging. Never required.
  context   String?
  status    SupportMessageStatus @default(OPEN)
  createdAt DateTime             @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime             @updatedAt
  resolvedAt DateTime?
  user      User                 @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([status, createdAt])
  @@index([userId, createdAt])
}
```

3. Add the back-relation on `model User` (schema.prisma:11-54) -- add a line `supportMessages SupportMessage[]` grouped with the other one-to-many report/flag relations (near `fieldIssueReportFlags` at line 36). Exact alignment doesn't matter, `npx prisma format` will fix column spacing.

4. From `server/`, run `npx prisma migrate dev --name add_support_messages` (requires `DIRECT_DATABASE_URL` per `.cursor/rules/prisma-db.mdc` -- this generates the migration SQL file under `server/prisma/migrations/` automatically, do not hand-write it) and then `npx prisma generate` so the local `@prisma/client` has the new model before task 2/3 write code against `prisma.supportMessage`.

Do not touch any other model or enum in this file.

title: Server: POST /api/support endpoint for submitting a bug report or message
Server: admin list + resolve endpoints for support messages
Web: API client wrapper for support messages
Web: feedback/bug-report dialog reachable from the footer
description:
Depends on task 4. Add the entry point the user asked for on web -- "probably the footer".

1. Create `next_app/src/components/SupportFeedbackDialog.tsx`: a self-contained trigger button + MUI `Dialog` (follow the Dialog/TextField/Select structure already used in `next_app/src/components/FieldIssueReportSection.tsx` around lines 294,389,429-442, but simpler -- no photo upload). Needs `useAuth`/`useUser` from `@clerk/nextjs` (same as `admin/moderation/page.tsx`) to get a token; if signed out, render a `SignInButton` inside the dialog instead of the form (mirror `next_app/src/app/admin/layout.tsx:36-45`'s signed-out card copy/pattern). Fields: a `Select` for type ("דיווח על באג" = BUG, "משוב כללי" = FEEDBACK), a multiline `TextField` for the message (required, mirror `MAX_TEXT_LENGTH`-style client-side cap at 2000 chars to match task 2's server cap), a Submit button calling `supportApi.submit({ type, message, context: window.location.pathname }, token)`, loading/error state, and a success `Alert`/snackbar that closes the dialog after a short delay (mirror `showSuccess` pattern at `FieldIssueReportSection.tsx:80`). Export a default component `SupportFeedbackDialog` that renders its own trigger `Typography`/`Button` styled like the existing `LINKS.map(...)` entries in `Footer.tsx` (component="button", same `variant="body2"`/color/hover styling as the other footer links) plus the `Dialog`, so `Footer.tsx` only needs to render `<SupportFeedbackDialog />` with no extra state of its own.

2. In `next_app/src/components/Footer.tsx`, add `<SupportFeedbackDialog />` into the first `Stack` (the one containing `LINKS.map(...)` and the `תמיכה` mailto link, lines 51-72) -- place it right after the `תמיכה` mailto `Typography` (around line 72), as a new item in that same row. Keep the existing `תמיכה` mailto link as-is (it stays as the no-login-required fallback for signed-out visitors); this dialog is the additional structured, trackable path. Add the import `import SupportFeedbackDialog from "@/components/SupportFeedbackDialog";` at the top.

title: Web: admin page to view and resolve support messages
description:
Depends on task 4. Add the admin-facing display the user asked for, following the exact pattern of the existing `moderation` admin route.

1. Create `next_app/src/app/admin/feedback/loading.tsx`, copying `next_app/src/app/admin/moderation/loading.tsx` verbatim except the label text (e.g. `label="טוען פניות…"`).

2. Create `next_app/src/app/admin/feedback/page.tsx`: a client component following `next_app/src/app/admin/moderation/page.tsx`'s structure (load-on-mount via `useAuth().getToken()`, `useState`/`useCallback`, `Card`/`CardContent`/`Chip`/`Stack` layout -- no `useIsAdmin` call needed, `admin/layout.tsx` already gates every child route). Use `supportApi.adminList(token)` to load into state, render each `SupportMessage` as a `Card` showing a `Chip` for `type` ("באג" for BUG / "משוב" for FEEDBACK) and one for `status`, the submitter's `user.name || user.id`, the `message` text (`whiteSpace: "pre-wrap"`, mirror moderation page.tsx:263), `context` if present as a caption, and (for `OPEN` rows only) a "סמן כטופל" button calling `supportApi.adminResolve(id, token)` then removing/updating that row in state -- mirror `handleDismiss` at `moderation/page.tsx:93-104` for the acting-state/error-handling shape. Show an `Alert severity="success"` empty state when there are no OPEN rows left (mirror `moderation/page.tsx:253-255`).

3. In `next_app/src/app/admin/layout.tsx`, add `{ href: "/admin/feedback", label: "פניות ודיווחי באגים" }` to the `ADMIN_TABS` array (layout.tsx:19-22), after the existing `moderation` entry.

title: Mobile: feedback/bug-report screen + entry point in Settings
description:
Depends on task 7 (API) and task 8 (i18n keys). This is the "where in mobile" entry point -- inside Settings, next to Privacy Policy / Terms of Service, matching the existing "App Info, Support" section.

1. Create `mobile_app/app/settings/feedback.tsx`, mirroring `mobile_app/app/profile/settings.tsx`'s screen shell (header row with back-chevron + centered title at lines 86-92, `SafeAreaView`, `useAuth`/`useUser` from `@clerk/clerk-expo`, `useTranslation`). Body: two selectable type pills (BUG / FEEDBACK, mirror the selectable-row style at `settings.tsx:105-121` or the filter-pill style at `mobile_app/app/fields/index.tsx`'s sport filter chips), a multiline `TextInput` (`multiline`, `numberOfLines={6}`, bg-white rounded border, matching this codebase's form-input styling) bound to a `message` state, and a submit `TouchableOpacity` styled like `settings.tsx:125-135`'s save button, calling `supportApi.submit({ type, message, context: 'mobile:/settings/feedback' }, token)` from the task-7 API module (import via `@/services/api`), then `Alert.alert('', t('feedback.success'))` and `router.back()` on success, or `Alert.alert(t('error', 'Error'), t('feedback.failure'))` on failure -- mirror `settings.tsx:63-83`'s try/catch/finally + `saving` state shape exactly. Disable submit while `message` is empty or a request is in flight.

2. In `mobile_app/app/settings/index.tsx`, add a new row to the "App Info, Support" card (settings/index.tsx:115-134), before the existing Privacy Policy row (line 116): a `TouchableOpacity` with `className="p-4 border-b border-gray-100 flex-row items-center justify-between"`, `onPress={() => router.push('/settings/feedback' as any)}`, containing `<Text className="text-base text-gray-800">{t('settings.feedback', 'Report a Bug / Contact Us')}</Text>` and the same trailing `<FontAwesome name="angle-right" ...>` chevron used by the two rows below it.

title: Mobile: admin screen to view and resolve support messages
description:
Depends on task 7. Mobile counterpart of task 6's web admin page, mirroring `mobile_app/app/admin/moderation.tsx`'s structure exactly (it's already gated by `mobile_app/app/admin/_layout.tsx`, no extra `useIsAdmin` call needed in the screen itself; imports come from the barrel `@/services/api` per moderation.tsx:7-12).

1. Create `mobile_app/app/admin/feedback.tsx`: same header-with-back-button shell as `moderation.tsx`, load `supportApi.adminList(token)` on mount into state (mirror `moderation.tsx:38-58`'s `load` callback shape), render each row as a card showing type ("באג"/"משוב"), status, submitter name/id, the message text, and (for OPEN rows) a "סמן כטופל" button calling `supportApi.adminResolve(id, token)` then removing it from local state or flipping its status in place -- mirror `moderation.tsx`'s dismiss-handler pattern (busyId/loading state, try/catch with `Alert.alert` on failure) for whichever handler follows the snippet at line 60 onward. Empty state: plain centered `Text` (e.g. "אין פניות פתוחות") when there are no OPEN rows, matching this screen's existing empty-state convention.

2. In `mobile_app/app/admin/index.tsx`, add a third entry to the `items` array (index.tsx:15-18): `{ title: 'פניות ודיווחי באגים', subtitle: 'הודעות משתמשים ודיווחי באגים', icon: 'comment', href: '/admin/feedback' }` (also widen that array's `href` union type to include `'/admin/feedback'`).
